t046: The vision, mission and scientific direction of LINK-ITALIA & PARTNERS.
t049: A project that brings together professional experience, research, awareness-raising and training to understand and address the LINK phenomenon.
t052: LINK-ITALIA & PARTNERS is a training and consultancy company that builds skills and active responsibility towards people and animals.
t053: Our approach starts from understanding the connections between animal abuse, interpersonal violence and other antisocial behaviour. The work focuses on prevention, attention to context and cooperation between disciplines.
t054: The We Break THE LINK® – One Safety, One Health, One Welfare® programme offers learning pathways and certification standards for individuals and organisations.
t058: In the Zooanthropology of Deviance, LINK refers to the correlation between the abuse and/or killing of animals, interpersonal violence and other deviant, antisocial or criminal behaviour. The concept underpins the study and training work of the LINK-ITALIA Project.

t211: Structure of the We Break THE LINK® programme and its training levels.
t214: A pathway to develop knowledge, professional sensitivity and competences on the LINK phenomenon, combining theory, awareness and practice.
t217: The aim is to improve the ability to prevent, recognise and counter violence from an inter-species perspective.
t218: The programme addresses the LINK phenomenon from a zooanthropological perspective and encourages cooperation between professionals, educational settings and organisations.
t219: The project has two levels: Level I, which builds social and professional knowledge and sensitivity, and Level II, which develops technical competences for qualified professionals.
t220: Organisations can also use our consultancy services: guidelines and protocols, analysis of LINK cases, support in setting up prevention systems, and assessment of the social dangerousness of acts against animals.

t237: A vision in which the safety, health and welfare of people, animals and the environment depend on one another.
t245: Violence has very high social costs.
t246: Violence takes a heavy toll on people’s health, on health and social services, on the justice system and on productivity. The 2014 report on violence prevention by the WHO, UNDP and UNODC, the analyses of the Copenhagen Consensus and European and Italian estimates show that prevention costs far less than intervening afterwards.
t247: Training people who work with people and animals to recognise the LINK is one of the most effective ways to intervene early.
